differences: Q01 has a higher spectral centroid (369.8 Hz versus 212.5 Hz), different prominent tones (Q01: 92.0, 109.8, 219.6 and 452.0 Hz; R01: 45.9, 85.9, 101.2 and 211.7 Hz), and a different harmonic-spacing pattern.
Q01 lacks R01's strong normalized 4–16 kHz envelope-line structure; its band-envelope modulation is weaker and distributed differently.
similarities: R01 is decisively closest in the PSD-estimator, physical-STFT, reassigned-STFT, wavelet and cepstral controls; those views consistently show the same comparatively broadband, higher-floor acquisition regime.
Both signals are unclipped, have similar RMS after peak normalization (0.243 versus 0.241 FS), similar crest factor (11.86 versus 11.93 dB), and near-Gaussian AC kurtosis (2.97 versus 2.87).
Both have weak filter-bank impulsiveness compared with most fault references and nearly fully populated cyclic maps without the extensive high-carrier masking seen in several alternatives.

differences: R02 is dominated by a strong 45.1 Hz component and low-frequency harmonic family, with much lower spectral centroid (51.8 Hz); Q01 instead has strongest listed tones at 92.0, 109.8, 219.6 and 452.0 Hz and centroid 369.8 Hz.
R02's 100–500 Hz envelope has strong 15 and 90.2 Hz modulation, unlike Q01's strongest 109.8 Hz modulation.
PSD/time-frequency controls place R02 substantially farther from Q01 than R01.
similarities: Both are unclipped and contain some approximately 30–31 Hz spectral spacing.

differences: R03 has strong 15 Hz modulation across several carrier bands and markedly positive broadband high-frequency filter-bank kurtosis; Q01 does not reproduce that cross-band 15 Hz signature and has near-zero filter-bank kurtosis.
R03 is low-frequency tonal with centroid 54.6 Hz, while Q01 is broader and has centroid 369.8 Hz.
R03's cyclic control is the most distant of all references.
similarities: Both contain peaks compatible with an approximately 30 Hz spacing, but peak-pair spacing alone is non-diagnostic.

differences: R04 has strong 29.9/30 Hz modulation in the broadband and 500–1500 Hz envelopes plus strong 30.4 Hz modulation in 4–8 kHz; Q01 instead emphasizes 109.8 Hz in 100–500 Hz and 123.2 Hz in 4–8 kHz.
R04's low-frequency 44.9/74.8 Hz tonal dominance and 65.9 Hz centroid differ from Q01's higher-frequency spectral distribution.
PSD and time-frequency controls are substantially farther than R01.
similarities: Both show occasional waveform-level changes, but their timing and modulation structure conflict.

differences: R05 has a highly concentrated 29.9–30.0 Hz modulation in 4–8 kHz and related 89.8 Hz modulation above 8 kHz; Q01 instead has weaker 61.6/123.2/246.3 Hz structure and no comparable 30 Hz dominance in those bands.
R05 is dominated by 43.9 Hz with centroid 56.6 Hz, unlike Q01's broad higher-frequency spectrum.
R05's PSD/time-frequency controls are substantially farther from Q01.
similarities: Both are unclipped and show low filter-bank impulsiveness over many bands.

differences: R06 exhibits strong 15 Hz modulation in the 100–500 Hz and 8–16 kHz envelopes and about 30 Hz in 500–1500 Hz; Q01 does not reproduce this cross-band pattern.

Although R06 is the nearest mean-centered Welch baseline, its estimator, detailed-STFT, reassigned and wavelet controls are much farther than R01, so baseline proximity is conflicting rather than decisive.
R06's centroid is 62.0 Hz and its low-frequency 44.9/29.9 Hz tones dominate, unlike Q01.
similarities: R06 is the closest reference under the single mean-centered full-band Welch baseline and has comparable high valid-cell coverage in cyclic coherence.

differences: R07 has strong 15.3 and 91.8 Hz modulation in 100–500 Hz, 62.3 Hz in 4–8 kHz, and 187 Hz above 8 kHz; Q01's corresponding pattern is 109.8, 123.2 and 61.6 Hz with much weaker high-band modulation.
R07 is dominated by 45.9 Hz and has centroid 57.6 Hz, unlike Q01's higher-frequency spectrum.
R07 is the farthest baseline/PSD/time-frequency candidate overall.
similarities: Both contain an approximately 30–31 Hz spacing family, but their prominent tones and carrier-band modulation disagree.

differences: R08 has concentrated 30.3/60.5–60.6 Hz modulation in 4–8 kHz and 181.7 Hz above 8 kHz; Q01 instead emphasizes 123.2/246.3 Hz in 4–8 kHz and 61.6 Hz above 8 kHz.
R08 is dominated by 44.6 Hz with centroid 54.3 Hz; Q01 has no comparable dominant 44–45 Hz tone and is much broader.
R08's PSD/time-frequency controls are substantially farther than R01, and neither filter-bank nor spectral kurtosis supplies a distinctive shared impact signature.
similarities: Both are unclipped and have low-to-mild filter-bank excess kurtosis rather than the strongly positive pattern of R03 or R06.

decision.explanation: Initial priorities were the reference-discriminating PSD/time-frequency shape, carrier-band modulation and impulsiveness views. The final decision is driven by the numerical controls: R01 is consistently nearest in estimators, physical STFT, reassigned STFT, wavelet and cepstrum, and Q01 also closely matches R01's normalized waveform statistics. The strongest counterevidence is that the mean-centered Welch baseline alone ranks R06 nearest and that Q01's spectral centroid and prominent tones differ substantially from R01; therefore this is supported condition-level similarity, not recording identity or proof of health. Envelope and harmonic views are mixed and correlated with the same underlying spectrum, so they were not treated as independent votes. Orders and synchronous averaging are unavailable for Q01 and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied; those views provide no evidence. No severity claim is supportable because recordings are peak-normalized and acquisition response/placement remain uncontrolled.
